public_rationale: The evidence does not establish that a vast majority of the relevant spending remains undeployed. Alphabet discloses substantial assets awaiting service, but also a larger gross in-service asset balance. Neither balance supplies the missing spending-cohort reconciliation. A low D&A-to-current-capex ratio cannot by itself identify the undeployed share: it compares an expense allocated over asset lives with current spending. That weakness in the argument does not prove the underlying claim false.
limitations: Evidence is incomplete across the four companies.
The outcome depends on a spending period and denominator the speaker did not specify.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Hyperscaler depreciation suggests the vast majority of their capex has not yet been put into service.

statement.excerpt: As I discussed a few months ago, despite vast amounts of capital expenditures, hyperscaler depreciation — by which I mean when you spread out the cost of GPUs over 6 years starting from when they enter service — also suggests that the vast majority of capex is yet to be put in service.

criteria.support_condition: A reconciliation of relevant spending cohorts, assets placed in service and assets awaiting service shows that a clearly dominant share remains undeployed across the named hyperscalers.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A comparable reconciliation shows that most relevant spending has entered service. Merely demonstrating that D&A divided by current capex is an invalid estimator does not establish the opposite factual outcome.
